present: 在场的；出席的；呈现；展示

stories.title: The Taste Test
stories.picture: 早市的果酱摊前，女孩把一小块面包递给摊主，旁边摆着蔬菜和烤火鸡。
paragraphs: At the morning market, Lin helped her aunt sell jam.
早市上，林帮姑姑卖果酱。
Their stall was busy, but nobody bought the new orange flavour.
她们的摊位很热闹，但没有人买新出的橙子口味。
Lin put small pieces of bread on a tray.
林把小块面包放在托盘上。
She invited people to dip a piece into a little pot.
她请大家把一块面包蘸进一个小罐里。
One man touched the bread with his tongue and frowned.
一个男人用舌头碰了碰面包，皱起眉头。
The taste was mild, but there was too much orange skin.
味道不浓，但橙皮太多了。
Her aunt changed the recipe and served it with turkey at lunch.
姑姑改了配方，午饭时用它来搭配火鸡肉。
By afternoon, shoppers were buying it along with the fresh produce.
到了下午，顾客买新鲜农产品时，也会买上一些。

stories.title: A Map with Two Homes
stories.picture: 教室里，一个女孩指着太平洋地图，桌上放着家乡和海外城市的照片。
paragraphs: Before moving abroad, Mei thought an ocean was just empty water.
搬到国外之前，梅以为海洋只是一片空旷的水域。
Her family would fly across the Pacific to their new home.
她一家将乘飞机飞越太平洋，前往新家。
At school, she marked their route on a large map.
在学校，她在大地图上标出了他们的路线。
Then a European classmate pointed to the place where he had lived.
接着，一位欧洲同学指了指他以前住过的地方。
It was a small village, not a famous capital.
那是一个小村庄，不是著名的首都。
Mei added a photo of her own village in a southern province.
梅又贴上了自己位于南方某省的村子的照片。
Another child added an island and the ferry to the mainland.
另一个孩子添上了一座岛和通往大陆的渡轮。
Soon the map showed not just distances, but connections between families.
很快，这张地图展现的不只是距离，还有家庭之间的联系。

stories.title: The Unfinished Letter
stories.picture: 纪念馆的玻璃展柜前，祖孙两人看着一封旧信，窗外有一门旧炮。
paragraphs: At a war memorial, Jun found a letter with no ending.
在一座战争纪念馆里，俊发现了一封没有结尾的信。
Its writer had carried a wounded man away from a bridge.
写信人曾把一个受伤的人从桥边背走。
Only later did he learn that the man was an enemy soldier.
后来他才知道，那个人是一名敌军士兵。
A comrade had asked why he had taken such a risk.
一位战友曾问他为什么冒这样的险。
The reply spoke of a brotherhood wider than any army.
回信谈到了一种超越任何军队界限的兄弟情谊。
Outside, an old cannon stood silent in the rain.
外面，一门旧大炮静静地立在雨中。
Jun left a white flower beside the writer's tomb.
俊在写信人的墓旁放了一朵白花。
He could not finish the letter, but he understood its message.
他无法替那封信写上结尾，却明白了信中的意思。

stories.title: A Song without a Star
stories.picture: 小剧场里，穿戏服的孩子们围着一位银发女歌手练习，钢琴旁亮着暖灯。
paragraphs: Our music teacher once sang in an opera company.
我们的音乐老师曾在一个歌剧团唱歌。
Before that, she worked evenings at a night-club to pay for lessons.
在那之前，她晚上在一家夜总会工作，以支付上课的费用。
She rarely spoke about fame, but loved helping beginners.
她很少谈名气，却喜欢帮助初学者。
For our first performance, she repaired an old costume herself.
为我们的第一次演出，她亲手修补了一套旧戏服。
I had a short dialogue with another child before the music began.
音乐开始前，我要和另一个孩子说一小段对白。
When I forgot my line, the teacher gave me a quiet cue.
我忘词时，老师悄悄给了我一个提示。
Then we all sang a tune that the youngest children knew.
接着，我们一起唱了一支连最小的孩子也熟悉的曲子。
The applause was for everyone, which was exactly what she wanted.
掌声属于所有人，这正是她所希望的。

stories.title: The Wrong Answer Wall
stories.picture: 教室后墙贴着彩色纸，学生们正微笑着讨论一张写错的练习。
paragraphs: Our teacher tried a new approach to mistakes.
老师尝试了一种对待错误的新方法。
After a quiz, each of us chose one wrong answer to discuss.
一次小测验后，我们每人选一道错题来讨论。
I brought a sheet from last week's dictation.
我带来了上周的一张听写纸。
A classmate brought a funny sentence from her composition.
一位同学带来了她作文里一个好笑的句子。
Someone else had used an idiom in completely the wrong situation.
还有人把一个习语用在了完全不合适的情境里。
We treated each mistake like a riddle, looking for the reason behind it.
我们把每个错误当作一个谜语，寻找背后的原因。
For homework, I wrote an essay about why errors are useful.
课后作业中，我写了一篇关于错误为什么有用的文章。
For once, I was not afraid to let the whole class read it.
这一次，我不再害怕让全班读我的文章了。

stories.title: The Bus That Waited
stories.picture: 雨中的窄路上，公交司机从驾驶室望向路边，老人正拎着袋子赶来。
paragraphs: At the station, a guard warned our driver about a fallen tree.
车站里，一名保安提醒我们的司机，路上有一棵倒下的树。
From his cab, the driver studied the narrow road ahead.
司机从驾驶室里仔细查看前方狭窄的道路。
He took a quiet lane instead of the usual main road.
他没有走平常的大路，而是拐进了一条安静的小路。
Near a bend, an old woman waved both arms at us.
在一处弯道附近，一位老太太向我们挥动双臂。
Beside her was a heavy load of bags and boxes.
她身旁是一大堆沉重的袋子和箱子。
The driver stopped well before her, avoiding a possible crash.
司机在离她还很远的地方就停了车，避免了可能发生的碰撞。
Two passengers helped her carry everything onto the bus.
两名乘客帮她把所有东西搬上了车。
We arrived late, but nobody asked him to drive faster.
我们到得晚了，但没有人要求他开快些。

stories.title: The Empty Boat
stories.picture: 湖边救援队员站在岸上拉绳，远处漂着一条空木船，孩子躲在树后。
paragraphs: A child's shout brought the rescue team to the lake.
一个孩子的喊声把救援队引到了湖边。
An empty boat was drifting away, and one end began to sink.
一条空船正向远处漂去，一端开始下沉。
The captain ordered everyone to stay on the bank.
队长命令所有人留在岸上。
He threw a rope across the boat and slowly pulled it back.
他把一根绳子抛到船的另一侧，慢慢把船拉了回来。
They searched for a victim, but found only a schoolbag.
他们寻找遇险者，却只找到一个书包。
Finally, a boy found the courage to step out from behind a tree.
终于，一个男孩鼓起勇气，从树后走了出来。
He had pushed the boat away and then tried to escape blame.
他推走了船，之后又试图逃避责备。
The team explained that their duty was to save lives, not punish children.
队员们解释说，他们的职责是救人，而不是惩罚孩子。

stories.title: A Garden in Space
stories.picture: 科学展桌上放着透明种植盒，学生用相机记录幼苗，后方屏幕显示宇航员。
paragraphs: A video of an astronaut growing lettuce started our project.
一段宇航员种生菜的视频开启了我们的项目。
Could we invent a watering box for a very small room?
我们能不能发明一种适用于狭小房间的浇水箱呢？
Our science teacher lent us some simple equipment.
科学老师借给我们一些简单的设备。
We used a camera to record how quickly each plant grew.
我们用照相机记录每株植物的生长速度。
At first, our invention gave the roots far too much water.
起初，我们的发明给根部浇了太多的水。
We changed the holes and repeated the test to prove that it worked.
我们改变了孔洞，然后重复试验来证明它有效。
A visitor noticed its potential for growing vegetables in city flats.
一位参观者注意到它在城市公寓里种菜的潜在用途。
We had begun with space, but could now imagine helping our neighbours.
我们的起点是太空，如今却能设想用它帮助邻居了。

stories.title: The Last Seat
stories.picture: 社区合唱排练室里，男孩把空椅子推向一位刚到的同学，两人露出笑容。
paragraphs: I used to envy the best singer in our club.
我曾经羡慕我们社团里唱得最好的人。
When he arrived late, I did not greet him as usual.
他迟到时，我没有像平常那样跟他打招呼。
I left my bag on the last empty chair.
我把书包放在了最后一张空椅子上。
He called this rude, and we began a quarrel.
他说这样很无礼，我们便争吵起来。
I wanted to complain about all the solos he received.
我想抱怨他总是获得独唱的机会。
But I was certain that hiding the chair would not improve my singing.
但我很清楚，霸占椅子并不能提高我的歌唱水平。
I offered an apology and moved my bag.
我道了歉，移开了书包。
His polite reply surprised me even more than his beautiful voice.
他有礼貌的回答，比他优美的歌声更让我惊讶。

stories.title: Grandmother's Workroom
stories.picture: 奶奶坐在缝纫桌旁，膝上放着布料，孩子把纽扣分进小盒子。
paragraphs: Grandmother calls herself a retired housewife, but her days are busy.
奶奶说自己是个退休的家庭主妇，但她的日子很忙。
A pile of old clothes waits beside her sewing machine.
缝纫机旁，一堆旧衣服正等着她处理。
She makes them into useful things that we can wear again.
她把它们改成我们可以重新穿戴的实用物品。
Yesterday, I watched her hold a soft cushion on her lap.
昨天，我看着她把一个柔软的靠垫放在膝上。
She showed me how to tuck the loose cloth inside.
她教我怎样把松开的布边塞进去。
I helped tidy the buttons into little boxes.
我帮忙把纽扣整理到小盒子里。
Even the cracked vase on her table held scraps of colourful thread.
就连她桌上那个有裂纹的花瓶，也装着零碎的彩色线头。
Nothing in that room seemed ready to be thrown away.
那个房间里似乎没有任何东西该被扔掉。

stories.title: A Place to Play
stories.picture: 小镇公共会议室里，学生举着旧球场照片向居民发言，窗外有高楼。
paragraphs: Our town planned to replace an old basketball court with a car park.
我们镇打算把一个旧篮球场改成停车场。
I had never been interested in local politics before.
在那之前，我对地方政治从不感兴趣。
This time, my friends asked me to attend a public meeting.
这一次，朋友们叫我去参加一场公开会议。
It would be held on the twentieth of May.
会议定在五月二十日举行。
During the debate, residents explained why both spaces were needed.
辩论中，居民们解释了为什么这两种场地都有必要。
I stood up to state how far children would have to walk to play.
我站起来说明，孩子们将不得不走多远才能打球。
Several parents present nodded when I showed them our photos.
我向大家展示照片时，几位在场的家长点了点头。
The council agreed to look for another place for the cars.
地方议会同意为汽车另找一个地方。

stories.title: The Fox under the Bridge
stories.picture: 小桥下，一只狐狸缩在泥岸上，穿雨靴的女孩蹲在桥栏边保持安静。
paragraphs: A red tail moved below the little bridge.
小桥下，一条红色的尾巴动了动。
I stopped so quickly that one boot filled with muddy water.
我停得太急，一只靴子里灌满了泥水。
A fox was trying to bury a piece of food in the bank.
一只狐狸正试着把一块食物埋进河岸。
I wanted to call my brother, but did not want to frighten it.
我想叫弟弟来看，却不愿吓到它。
We watched from a dry spot beside the path.
我们从小路旁一处干燥的地方看着它。
A nearby swing began to shake in the wind.
附近的一架秋千开始在风中晃动。
Then we heard a loose branch strike the wooden seat.
接着，我们听见一根松动的树枝打在木座上。
The fox vanished, leaving us with only a story to tell.
狐狸消失了，只给我们留下了一个可以讲述的故事。

stories.title: The Missing Coat
stories.picture: 旧教堂门边，一个戴领带的男孩把外套交给老人，走廊深处透进夕阳。
paragraphs: After a concert at the old church, a man could not find his coat.
旧教堂的音乐会结束后，一个男人找不到自己的外套了。
I saw him searching the long corridor outside the hall.
我看见他在大厅外的长走廊里寻找。
He wore a bright necktie that was easy to remember.
他戴着一条鲜亮的领带，很容易辨认。
Just before the doors shut, I noticed a coat under a chair.
就在门关上之前，我注意到椅子下面有一件外套。
Did it belong to him or to one of the musicians?
它是他的，还是某位乐手的呢？
I checked a photo that Dad had taken before the concert.
我查看了爸爸在音乐会前拍的一张照片。
In that shot, the man was holding exactly the same coat.
在那张照片里，那个男人拿着完全相同的外套。
We caught up with him before he walked out into the cold.
他还没走到寒冷的室外，我们就追上了他。

stories.title: More than a Famous Name
stories.picture: 图书馆里，女孩翻看旧账本，墙上挂着一位早期女商人的画像。
paragraphs: For a history project, I studied a pioneer of the local tea trade.
做历史项目时，我研究了本地茶叶贸易的一位开拓者。
A book described her rise from a poor family.
一本书描述了她如何从贫困家庭中崛起。
It called her life a splendid tale of personal success.
书中把她的一生称为一个精彩的个人成功故事。
Then I found an old account book in the library.
后来，我在图书馆发现了一本旧账本。
It recorded wages paid to a servant who had travelled with her.
里面记录了付给一位随她出行的仆人的工资。
Their journeys had been tough, with little food and dangerous roads.
他们的旅途十分艰难，食物短缺，道路危险。
Yet the famous biography never mentioned this helper's name.
然而，那本著名的传记从未提到这位帮手的名字。
I decided my report should make room for more than one person.
我决定，我的报告不应该只写一个人。

stories.title: The First Question
stories.picture: 教室里，女孩举起手询问，老师停下板书，周围同学转头认真倾听。
paragraphs: Lately, our teacher had noticed how quiet I was in class.
最近，老师注意到我在课堂上非常安静。
Whenever I was confused, I copied others instead of asking.
每当我感到困惑时，我都照抄别人的，而不提问。
One morning, an instruction on the board made no sense to me.
一天早上，黑板上的一条指示让我摸不着头脑。
I did not dare raise my hand at first.
起初，我不敢举手。
I moved my pencil back and forth, hoping someone else would speak.
我来回挪动着铅笔，希望别人会开口。
Eventually, I asked what the first step meant.
最终，我问第一步是什么意思。
Three classmates immediately said that they had the same problem.
三位同学立刻说，他们也有同样的问题。
It was a small matter, but it changed how I felt about questions.
这是一件小事，却改变了我对提问的感受。

stories.title: Dinner after the Snow
stories.picture: 社区厨房里，志愿者把热饭放上托盘，门外台阶积着白雪。
paragraphs: Snow kept many older neighbours indoors, so our class cooked dinner for them.
大雪让许多老邻居无法出门，于是我们班为他们做晚饭。
A farmer gave us fresh produce that he could not deliver.
一位农民把他无法送出的新鲜农产品给了我们。
We bought a turkey with money from our school craft stall.
我们用学校手工摊位挣来的钱买了一只火鸡。
The cook chose a mild sauce because some people disliked hot food.
厨师选了一种口味温和的酱汁，因为有些人不喜欢辣的食物。
I learned to dip a clean spoon into the sauce to taste it.
我学着把一把干净的勺子伸进酱汁里试味。
It was too hot and nearly burned my tongue.
酱汁太烫，差点烫伤了我的舌头。
Later, each tray carried a warm meal and a bread roll.
后来，每个托盘上都放着一份热饭和一个小面包。
A neighbour sent us homemade jam in return the next morning.
第二天早上，一位邻居送来了自制果酱作为回礼。

stories.title: Why the Birds Stop Here
stories.picture: 海边湿地，学生隔着围栏观察候鸟，老师指着鸟腿上的彩色环。
paragraphs: Every autumn, birds arrive on our island from abroad.
每年秋天，鸟儿从国外来到我们岛上。
They fly over the Pacific, stopping where they can find enough food.
它们飞越太平洋，在能找到足够食物的地方停留。
A European scientist helped our class study their journey.
一位欧洲科学家帮助我们班研究它们的旅程。
One bird carried a tiny device that recorded its route.
一只鸟身上带着一个记录路线的小装置。
It had passed close to a crowded capital without landing.
它曾从一座拥挤的首都附近经过，却没有降落。
Instead, it rested beside a quiet lake on the mainland.
相反，它在大陆上一个安静的湖边休息。
That lake lies in a province where many wetlands have disappeared.
那个湖位于一个已有许多湿地消失的省份。
Protecting one small area could therefore help birds on a much longer journey.
因此，保护一小片区域，就可能帮助远行的鸟儿。

stories.title: Two Names on One Stone
stories.topic: 一块石头上的两个名字
stories.picture: 山间步道旁，两名学生清理纪念石上的落叶，旁边的小牌展示着旧照片。
paragraphs: On a mountain walk, we found a memorial hidden by leaves.
山间徒步时，我们发现了一座被树叶遮住的纪念碑。
Two names were cut into the stone beside an empty tomb.
一座空墓旁的石头上刻着两个名字。
A local guide told us that one man had once been the other's enemy.
当地向导告诉我们，其中一人曾是另一人的敌人。
During a battle, a cannon had destroyed the path down the mountain.
一场战斗中，一门大炮炸毁了下山的路。
Both men were wounded and could only survive by helping each other.
两人都受了伤，只有互相帮助才能活下来。
Years later, one returned with a former comrade to search for the place.
多年以后，其中一人和一位从前的战友重返这里，寻找当年的地点。
They built this stone as a sign of brotherhood, not victory.
他们立下这块石碑，象征兄弟情谊，而不是胜利。
We cleared the leaves so that the next walkers could read both names.
我们清走了树叶，让下一批徒步者也能读到这两个名字。

stories.title: The Sound behind the Door
stories.picture: 旧音乐厅的资料室里，两个孩子戴着耳机听旧录音，桌上放着褪色演出照。
paragraphs: The building near our library used to be a night-club.
图书馆附近的那栋楼过去是一家夜总会。
Now it holds old recordings from the city's theatres.
如今，那里存放着这座城市各家剧院的老录音。
We listened to a young woman singing a tune that my grandfather knew.
我们听到一位年轻女子唱着一支爷爷熟悉的曲子。
In the next recording, she had a small part in an opera.
下一段录音中，她在一部歌剧里扮演一个小角色。
Her spoken dialogue sounded nervous, but her song was clear.
她说对白时听起来很紧张，但歌声十分清亮。
A bell was the cue for her to leave the stage.
一声铃响就是她退场的提示。
In a faded photo, she wore a costume made from cheap curtains.
一张褪色照片里，她穿着用廉价窗帘做成的戏服。
She never achieved great fame, yet her voice had survived for sixty years.
她从未大红大紫，但她的歌声却保存了六十年。

stories.title: The Dictionary Game
stories.picture: 图书角里，一群学生围着词典和答题纸，窗外下着细雨。
paragraphs: Rain cancelled our sports afternoon, so we made a language game.
下雨让下午的体育活动取消了，于是我们设计了一个语言游戏。
Each team received a sheet with an unfinished riddle.
每队拿到一张写着未完成谜语的纸。
The answer was hidden in an essay about animals.
答案藏在一篇关于动物的文章里。
To find it, we had to explain an idiom that contained a bird's name.
为了找到答案，我们得解释一个包含鸟名的习语。
My usual approach was to guess, but this time I opened a dictionary.
我平常的做法是猜，但这次我翻开了词典。
Next came a short dictation, which tested how carefully we listened.
接下来是一小段听写，考查我们听得是否仔细。
Our final task was a composition using the answer as its title.
最后一个任务是用答案作标题写一篇作文。
By the end, the room was louder than it had ever been during a quiz.
结束时，屋里比以往任何一次测验时都要热闹。

stories.title: The Parcel's Journey
stories.picture: 乡村小站外，送货员和保安一起检查一个压扁的纸箱，货车停在旁边。
paragraphs: My aunt's parcel arrived with one corner badly crushed.
姑姑的包裹送到时，一个角被压得很厉害。
The delivery driver feared that something had fallen from his load.
送货司机担心，他装载的货物里有东西掉下来砸到了包裹。
He checked the floor of the cab, but found no loose boxes.
他检查了驾驶室地板，却没发现散落的箱子。
Then a guard at the railway station remembered hearing a loud crash.
后来，火车站的一位保安想起曾听到一声巨响。
A large empty case had fallen off a shelf before the parcel was collected.
这个包裹被取走之前，一个大空箱曾从架子上掉下来。
The driver returned along the lane beside the tracks.
司机沿铁轨旁的小路返回。
He slowed at every bend, though the road was empty.
虽然路上没有车，他经过每一处弯道时仍然减速。
My aunt thanked him for finding the cause rather than blaming someone else.
姑姑感谢他查明了原因，而不是责怪别人。

stories.title: Rehearsal at the Pool
stories.picture: 室内泳池旁，救生教练指导学生向水中假人抛绳，其他人站在安全线后。
paragraphs: Our swimming lesson began with a rescue exercise.
我们的游泳课以一次救援演练开始。
The captain of the local rescue team placed a training dummy in the water.
当地救援队的队长把一个训练假人放进水中。
We watched it sink until only its bright head remained visible.
我们看着它下沉，直到只能看见颜色鲜亮的头部。
Our first duty was to call for adult help.
我们的首要责任是呼叫成年人来帮忙。
A loud shout was useful, but jumping in could put two people in danger.
大声呼喊是有用的，但跳下水可能让两个人都陷入危险。
Instead, we practised throwing a rope towards the victim from dry ground.
因此，我们练习从干燥的地面上向遇险者抛绳。
The coach explained how to escape someone's grip if they pulled us towards the edge.
教练解释了，如果有人把我们拉向池边，该如何挣脱对方的抓握。
I learned that courage can mean stopping yourself from doing something unsafe.
我明白了，勇气也可以意味着克制自己，不做不安全的事。

stories.title: A Button for Grandpa
stories.picture: 男孩坐在桌前测试大按钮，爷爷在旁微笑，桌上放着拆开的旧收音机。
paragraphs: Grandpa could no longer see the tiny buttons on his radio.
爷爷已经看不清收音机上那些细小的按钮了。
I wanted to invent a larger control that he could use by touch.
我想发明一个更大的控制装置，让他凭触摸就能使用。
I could imagine its shape, but knew little about wires.
我能想象出它的形状，却不太懂电线。
A repair shop lent me equipment and helped me build a safe model.
一家维修店借给我设备，帮我做出一个安全的模型。
The owner had once repaired a camera for a visiting astronaut.
店主曾给一位到访的宇航员修过照相机。
He said my simple invention also solved a real problem.
他说，我这个简单的发明同样解决了一个实际问题。
To prove its value, I asked Grandpa to try it without my help.
为了证明它的价值，我请爷爷不靠我帮忙试着使用它。
When he found his favourite programme, I understood the potential of a small idea.
他找到最喜欢的节目时，我明白了一个小想法的潜力。

stories.title: A Review Written Twice
stories.picture: 餐馆靠窗的桌边，一家人和服务员交谈，女孩把手机轻轻放下。
paragraphs: At a café, I waited a long time for my drink.
在一家咖啡馆里，我等了很久，饮料还没上来。
I was certain that the waiter had forgotten us.
我确信服务员把我们忘了。
I began writing a rude review on my phone.
我开始在手机上写一条措辞无礼的评价。
Dad suggested that I complain in person before posting it.
爸爸建议我先当面提出不满，再发布评价。
The waiter came to greet us and explained that a pipe had broken.
服务员过来招呼我们，解释说一根水管坏了。
His apology was so honest that I deleted my angry words.
他的道歉非常诚恳，于是我删掉了那些气话。
We did not need a quarrel to get a polite explanation.
我们不需要吵一架，也能得到有礼貌的解释。
I used to envy people who always won arguments, but now I was less sure.
我曾经羡慕那些争论总能获胜的人，但现在我不那么确定了。

stories.title: The Cat at the Repair Café
stories.picture: 社区修理角里，妇女补着靠垫，一只猫趴在她膝上，孩子整理旧衣服。
paragraphs: At our community repair café, people bring things they want to save.
在我们社区的修理角，人们会带来想要修好的东西。
A housewife named Mrs Chen teaches children simple sewing skills.
一位姓陈的家庭主妇教孩子们简单的缝纫技巧。
People bring shirts they still want to wear, although the sleeves are torn.
人们带来袖子破了却仍想穿的衬衫。
Last Saturday, she was repairing a cushion when a cat climbed onto her lap.
上周六，她正在修补一个靠垫，一只猫爬上了她的膝头。
Nobody wanted to move it, so I helped with the sewing.
谁也不想挪开它，于是我帮忙缝补。
She told me to tuck the sharp needle into a small cloth case afterwards.
她告诉我，用完后要把尖针插进一个小布套里。
Meanwhile, my brother made a pile of fabric bags to keep the table tidy.
与此同时，弟弟把布袋叠成一摞，让桌面保持整洁。
Someone even repaired a broken vase, although it could hold only dried flowers now.
还有人修好了一只破花瓶，虽然它现在只能插干花了。

stories.title: Reading the News Slowly
stories.picture: 课堂上，学生把报纸和地图铺在桌上，老师带着大家核对报道。
paragraphs: On the twentieth of March, our class began a news project.
三月二十日，我们班开始了一个新闻项目。
The first report concerned a court in a distant state.
第一篇报道涉及一个遥远州里的一家法院。
Several students thought the story was about our own town.
几个学生以为那篇报道说的是我们镇。
Our teacher asked everyone present to find the place on a map.
老师请所有在场的人在地图上找到那个地方。
Then we held a debate about how quickly false ideas spread.
接着，我们就错误观念的传播速度展开了辩论。
A local reporter agreed to attend our next lesson.
一位当地记者答应来参加我们的下一堂课。
She said that reports about politics need especially careful reading.
她说，有关政治的报道尤其需要仔细阅读。
We decided to check dates and places before sharing any surprising news.
我们决定，在转发任何惊人的消息前，先核对日期和地点。

stories.title: The Time Box
stories.picture: 校园大树下，学生把密封铁盒放进浅坑，旁边立着一双沾泥雨靴。
paragraphs: Our class chose a spot near the oldest tree for a time box.
我们班在最老的树旁选了一个地方，准备埋下时光盒。
We planned to bury letters there until we finished school.
我们打算把信埋在那里，直到毕业再取出来。
The hole was below the roots, so we moved it further away.
挖的坑在树根下方，于是我们把位置移得更远了些。
I pressed the loose earth down with the heel of my boot.
我用靴子的后跟把松土压实。
A younger child watched us from a swing beside the fence.
一个年纪小些的孩子在围栏旁的秋千上看着我们。
A sudden noise made him shake with fear.
一声突如其来的响声吓得他直发抖。
It was only a stone that had happened to strike our empty tin.
那不过是一块石头碰巧打中了我们的空铁罐。
We showed him inside the box so that our secret would not frighten him.
我们让他看了看盒子里面，免得这个秘密吓着他。

stories.title: The Photograph Nobody Wanted
stories.picture: 摄影展的走廊里，一名少年和老人停在一张旧街景照片前。
paragraphs: I entered a school photography show with a shot of a ruined building.
我用一张废弃建筑的照片参加了学校摄影展。
It had once been a church, but only one wall remained.
那里曾是一座教堂，但只剩下一面墙。
I thought the empty doorway made it look mysterious.
我觉得空空的门洞让它显得很神秘。
Before the exhibition shut, an old man stopped me in the corridor.
展览关闭前，一位老人在走廊里叫住了我。
He recognised a necktie hanging from a nail inside the doorway.
他认出了门洞里面钉子上挂着的一条领带。
It used to belong to his father, who had worked next door.
它以前属于他的父亲，他父亲曾在隔壁工作。
The building was not empty to him; it was full of memories.
对他来说，那栋建筑并不空，那里满是回忆。
I gave him a copy and changed the words beneath my picture.
我给了他一张照片，并改写了照片下方的说明。

stories.title: The Price of Cheap Cloth
stories.picture: 博物馆里，学生看着旧织机和工人的照片，讲解员手里拿着一块粗布。
paragraphs: A museum display celebrated a pioneer who had built the first local cloth factory.
博物馆的一个展览纪念了一位建造本地首家布厂的开拓者。
It showed how the cloth trade had brought money to the area.
展览展示了布匹贸易如何为当地带来收入。
A painting presented a splendid dinner in the owner's large house.
一幅画描绘了厂主大宅里的一场丰盛晚宴。
In one corner, a young servant waited beside the door.
画面一角，一个年轻仆人在门边等候。
I wondered what she would have said about that evening.
我想知道，她会如何讲述那个夜晚。
Another display described the tough conditions inside the factory.
另一个展区描述了工厂内艰苦的环境。
The guide said that every tale of progress has more than one side.
讲解员说，每一个关于进步的故事都有不止一个侧面。
I left wanting to learn about the workers as well as their employer.
离开时，我既想了解厂主，也想了解工人。

stories.title: Learning to Cycle Again
stories.picture: 公园空旷小路上，男孩扶着自行车，姐姐在前面回头鼓励他。
paragraphs: After a fall, my brother would not dare ride his bicycle.
摔倒以后，弟弟不敢再骑自行车了。
Lately, he had even stopped coming to the park.
最近，他甚至不再去公园了。
I found a flat path where traffic would not matter.
我找到了一条平坦的小路，在那里不必考虑车流。
My first instruction was simply to walk beside the bike.
我的第一条指示，只是让他推着车走。
He went back and forth until his shoulders relaxed.
他来回走着，直到肩膀放松下来。
Whenever he felt ready, he could put one foot on a pedal.
每当他感觉准备好了，就可以把一只脚放上踏板。
Eventually, both wheels rolled forward without my hand on the seat.
终于，在我没有扶着座椅的情况下，两个轮子向前滚动起来。
He travelled only a few metres, but they were his own.
他只骑了几米，但那是他自己骑出的几米。

stories.title: When Food Loses Its Smell
stories.picture: 科学活动室里，一个蒙眼的学生试吃小块食物，同学拿着记录表站在旁边。
paragraphs: In science club, we tested how smell changes the taste of food.
在科学社团里，我们测试了气味怎样改变食物的味道。
Our teacher placed cooked turkey and pieces of apple on a tray.
老师把熟火鸡肉和苹果块放在一个托盘上。
With my eyes covered and my nose held, I could feel food on my tongue.
蒙住眼睛、捏住鼻子后，我能感觉到舌头上的食物。
Yet it was surprisingly difficult to name a mild flavour.
然而，要辨认一种清淡的味道，竟然很难。
Next, I had to dip a fresh spoon into some strawberry jam.
接下来，我要用一把干净的勺子蘸一些草莓酱。
I recognised sweetness, but could not name the fruit until I released my nose.
我尝出了甜味，却直到松开鼻子才辨认出水果种类。
A grower at a nearby farm stall later let us compare different apples.
后来，附近一个农场摊位的种植者让我们比较了不同的苹果。
Fresh produce gave us far more to notice than colour alone.
新鲜农产品带给我们的感受，远不止颜色而已。

stories.title: A Bottle's Long Journey
stories.picture: 海滩清理活动中，两个孩子打开旧瓶子里的纸条，身后是蓝色海面。
paragraphs: While cleaning a beach, we found a sealed bottle from abroad.
清理海滩时，我们发现了一个来自国外的密封瓶子。
Inside was a message from a European family travelling by ship.
里面是一家欧洲人乘船旅行时留下的纸条。
They had thrown it into the Pacific twelve years earlier.
十二年前，他们把瓶子扔进了太平洋。
An ocean expert helped us guess its possible route.
一位海洋专家帮我们推测了它可能的漂流路线。
It might have passed the coast of our province several times.
它可能已经好几次经过了我们省的海岸。
A child asked whether it would be quicker to fly to the family.
一个孩子问，乘飞机去那一家人那里会不会更快。
The expert laughed, then showed us how rubbish reaches both islands and the mainland.
专家笑了，接着向我们展示垃圾怎样到达岛屿和大陆。
We sent our findings to an exhibition in the capital, along with a request for cleaner seas.
我们把发现连同保护海洋清洁的呼吁，一起送到了首都的一个展览上。

stories.title: The Veteran's Visitor
stories.picture: 明亮病房里，两位白发老人握手，床头摆着年轻时的黑白合照。
paragraphs: When my grandfather was in hospital, an unexpected visitor came to see him.
爷爷住院时，一位意想不到的访客来看他。
He was the son of a wounded soldier whom Grandfather had helped during a war.
他是一名士兵的儿子，爷爷曾在战争中救助过那位受伤的士兵。
The two older men had served on opposite sides, each calling the other an enemy.
那两位老人当年分属敌对阵营，都把对方称作敌人。
After the fighting, the men joined a rescue unit, and Grandfather began calling him a comrade.
战争结束后，两人加入了一支救援队，爷爷开始称他为战友。
They wrote letters for years, building a quiet brotherhood.
他们多年通信，建立起一份平静的兄弟情谊。
The visitor brought a photograph of his father's tomb and a small stone from home.
来客带来了一张父亲坟墓的照片和一块家乡的小石头。
He also brought a sketch of a cannon that both men remembered.
他还带来了一幅素描，画着两位老人都记得的一门大炮。
Grandfather said their letters were a better memorial than any weapon could be.
爷爷说，比起任何武器，他们的通信都更能纪念那段往事。

stories.title: Music You Can Feel
stories.picture: 无障碍音乐工作坊里，孩子把手放在共鸣木箱上，演员用手势示意开场。
paragraphs: A local singer offered a workshop for children who could not hear well.
一位本地歌手为听力不佳的孩子开办了一个工作坊。
He usually performed at a night-club, but today he wanted a quieter room.
他通常在一家夜总会演出，但这一天他想要一个更安静的房间。
He played a slow tune while we touched a wooden box beside the speaker.
他弹奏一支缓慢的曲子时，我们触摸着扬声器旁的一个木箱。
We could feel the low notes through our fingers.
我们能通过手指感受到低音。
A flash of light was our cue to begin a simple dance.
一道闪光就是我们开始跳简单舞步的提示。
An actor in a bright costume acted out a scene from an opera.
一名穿着鲜艳戏服的演员表演了歌剧中的一个场景。
The dialogue appeared on a screen, so everyone could follow the story.
对白显示在屏幕上，让每个人都能跟上故事。
The singer said that reaching new listeners mattered more to him than fame.
那位歌手说，对他而言，接触到新的听众比名气更重要。

stories.title: A Book in Two Voices
stories.picture: 祖孙坐在窗边，小女孩在纸上记下老人讲的故事，桌上放着装订小册子。
paragraphs: My grandfather wanted to write about his childhood, but his hands hurt.
爷爷想写写自己的童年，但他的手疼。
We chose a different approach: he talked while I wrote.
我们选了另一种方法：他讲，我写。
It felt like dictation, except that I could stop him with questions.
这感觉像听写，只不过我可以打断他提问。
Every sheet filled up with games, meals and names of old friends.
每张纸都写满了游戏、饭菜和老朋友的名字。
He explained an idiom that his mother had often used.
他解释了一个他母亲常用的习语。
He also taught me a riddle that became a quiz for our whole family.
他还教给我一个谜语，后来成了我们全家的小测验题。
I added a short composition describing our afternoons together.
我添了一篇短作文，描述我们一起度过的那些下午。
Our little book ended with his essay about why ordinary memories are worth keeping.
我们的小书以他的一篇文章收尾，主题是平凡的记忆为何值得保存。

stories.title: The Model Crossing
stories.picture: 科技教室里，学生围着铁路道口模型测试灯光，纸板卡车停在轨道前。
paragraphs: Our class built a model railway station for a safety exhibition.
我们班为安全展制作了一个火车站模型。
A toy truck carried a load of wooden blocks towards the tracks.
一辆玩具卡车载着木块驶向铁轨。
The driver in its tiny cab could not see a train around the bend.
小小驾驶室里的司机，看不到弯道另一边的火车。
We first placed a warning light too far down the lane.
起初，我们把警示灯放在小路上太靠前的位置。
By the time it flashed, the truck had already reached the crossing.
灯闪起来时，卡车已经到了道口。
There was a crash, and the blocks scattered across our table.
一声碰撞后，木块散落在我们的桌面上。
A real crossing guard helped us move the light to a safer position.
一位真正的道口看守员帮我们把灯移到了更安全的位置。
The next test showed why warning signs must give people time to act.
下一次测试表明了，警示标志为什么必须给人留下行动的时间。

stories.title: The Voice in the Dark
stories.picture: 录音室里，孩子对着麦克风演广播剧，另一人在水盆旁制造海浪声。
paragraphs: Our drama club made a radio play about a ship in trouble.
我们戏剧社制作了一部讲述船只遇险的广播剧。
I played the captain, whose duty was to get everyone safely ashore.
我扮演船长，他的职责是把所有人安全送上岸。
Because listeners could see nothing, every sound had to tell part of the story.
因为听众什么也看不到，每种声音都必须传达一部分情节。
My friend pulled a rope across wood to make the boat sound old.
朋友在木头上拉动绳子，让船听起来很破旧。
Another actor played a victim trapped in a room below the deck.
另一位演员扮演被困在甲板下房间里的遇险者。
As the ship began to sink, we heard his desperate shout.
船开始下沉时，我们听到了他绝望的喊声。
My character needed the courage to return for him instead of leaving alone.
我扮演的角色需要鼓起勇气回去救他，而不是独自离开。
When they finally made their escape, even our teacher let out a breath.
他们最终成功逃生时，连老师也松了一口气。

stories.title: A Picture Too Good to Be True
stories.picture: 电脑前，两名学生放大一张太空照片，旁边摆着相机和新闻核查笔记。
paragraphs: A picture online showed an astronaut holding a flower on the Moon.
网上的一张图片显示，一位宇航员正在月球上拿着一朵花。
The writer claimed that a new invention could grow flowers without water.
配文者声称，一项新发明能让花不需要水就生长。
I wanted to believe it and began to imagine colourful gardens in space.
我很想相信，还开始想象太空中五彩缤纷的花园。
My sister asked what evidence could prove the claim.
姐姐问，有什么证据能证明这个说法。
We found the original image on a camera maker's website.
我们在一家相机制造商的网站上找到了原图。
The flower had been added, and the equipment was actually being tested indoors.
花是后来加上的，而那些设备其实正在室内接受测试。
It is easy to invent an exciting story around a changed photograph.
围绕一张改过的照片编造一个精彩故事，并不难。
The potential harm is real when readers share it without checking.
读者不经核实就转发时，潜在的危害是真实存在的。

stories.title: The Tall Sunflowers
stories.picture: 两户人家的花园交界处，老人和女孩查看落在菜地上的向日葵影子。
paragraphs: Our neighbour grew sunflowers taller than our fence.
邻居种的向日葵长得比围栏还高。
Mum began to complain that their shadow covered her vegetables.
妈妈开始抱怨，花的影子遮住了她的蔬菜。
I expected a quarrel when she knocked on the neighbour's door.
她敲邻居家门时，我以为要吵架了。
Instead, she began with a polite question about his garden.
然而，她先有礼貌地问起了他的花园。
He came outside to greet us and looked at the dark patch himself.
他走出来招呼我们，亲自查看了那片阴影。
He offered an apology and promised to move some pots.
他道了歉，并答应挪动几个花盆。
I had thought him rude, but was no longer certain I had been fair.
我曾认为他无礼，现在却不确定自己的判断是否公正。
Now I envy Mum's ability to solve a problem without making an enemy.
现在，我羡慕妈妈不树敌也能解决问题的本领。

stories.title: A Day That Looked Like Rest
stories.picture: 餐桌边，女孩写采访记录，妈妈整理孩子的衣服，窗台上摆着花瓶。
paragraphs: For a school interview, I followed my mother through an ordinary day.
为了完成一次学校采访，我跟着妈妈度过了平常的一天。
She is a housewife, and I had thought that meant plenty of free time.
她是家庭主妇，我原以为那意味着很多空闲时间。
Before breakfast, she found clean clothes for my little brother to wear.
早餐前，她为弟弟找出了干净衣服来穿。
Then she washed a pile of dishes and tried to tidy the living room.
接着，她洗了一堆碗碟，又试着收拾客厅。
My brother knocked over a vase, so she had to clear the broken pieces.
弟弟撞倒了一个花瓶，她只好清理碎片。
Later, he fell asleep on her lap while she sat against a cushion.
后来，她靠着一个靠垫坐下，弟弟在她膝上睡着了。
I watched her tuck a blanket around him without waking him.
我看着她给他掖好毯子，没有吵醒他。
In my report, I called that quiet hour work, not rest.
在报告里，我把那安静的一小时称作工作，而不是休息。

stories.title: The Guest Chair
stories.picture: 模拟法庭上，学生坐成半圆，一位记者坐在留出的椅子上认真记录。
paragraphs: For our school's twentieth birthday, we held a mock trial.
为了庆祝学校二十岁生日，我们举行了一次模拟审判。
The case concerned a fictional town that wanted to cut down its oldest tree.
案件涉及一个虚构的小镇，那里打算砍掉最老的一棵树。
We arranged our classroom like a court, with seats for the public.
我们把教室布置成法庭的样子，留出了公众席位。
A reporter asked if she could attend as an observer.
一位记者问，她能否作为旁听者参加。
Everyone present had to listen without interrupting the speakers.
所有在场的人都必须认真听，不打断发言者。
At first, our debate sounded like an argument between friends.
起初，我们的辩论听起来像朋友间的争执。
Then the teacher reminded us to state our reasons and offer evidence.
接着，老师提醒我们要陈述理由并提供证据。
I realised that learning about politics could begin with learning how to listen.
我意识到，了解政治可以从学会倾听开始。

stories.title: After the Storm
stories.picture: 公园里，一名工作人员检查被树枝砸坏的秋千，孩子站在警示带外。
paragraphs: After the storm, I went to the park to look for my missing boot.
暴风雨过后，我到公园去找丢失的靴子。
Strong water had carried it away from our back step.
急流把它从我家后门台阶冲走了。
I found it below a broken branch near the playground.
我在游乐场附近的一根断枝下方找到了它。
The branch had fallen to strike a swing and crack its seat.
那根树枝掉下来砸中了秋千，砸裂了座板。
A worker asked us not to shake the damaged frame.
一名工作人员让我们不要摇晃损坏的支架。
He marked the spot so that nobody would try to play there.
他标出了那个地方，以免有人想在那里玩耍。
Then he noticed ants trying to bury their eggs in higher ground.
接着，他注意到蚂蚁正试着把卵埋进更高处的土里。
We stepped carefully around them, not wishing to frighten any more storm survivors.
我们小心地绕过它们，不想再惊吓这些从暴风雨中活下来的小生命。

stories.title: The Borrowed Building
stories.picture: 改建后的旧教堂里，学生拍摄短片，门外走廊贴着临时安静标识。
paragraphs: Our film club was allowed to use an old church for one afternoon.
我们电影社获准使用一座旧教堂一个下午。
It was now a community hall rather than a place of worship.
那里如今是社区活动厅，不再是礼拜场所。
The costumes did not belong to us, so we handled them carefully.
那些服装不属于我们，所以我们小心地使用。
My character was a shy clerk with an enormous necktie.
我扮演一名害羞的办事员，戴着一条特别大的领带。
For the final shot, I had to run along the corridor and knock on a door.
拍摄最后一个镜头时，我得沿着走廊跑过去敲门。
I pushed too hard, and the door swung shut behind me.
我推得太用力，门在我身后关上了。
My friends thought I was acting when I asked them to let me out.
我叫朋友们放我出去时，他们以为我在演戏。
We kept the mistake in the film because it made everyone laugh.
我们把这个失误保留在影片里，因为它让所有人都笑了。

stories.title: The Game Nobody Bought
stories.picture: 校园义卖桌前，两个学生把复杂棋盘收起，改用几张简单卡片邀请同学试玩。
paragraphs: For charity week, our group made a board game about the silk trade.
慈善周时，我们组制作了一款关于丝绸贸易的棋盘游戏。
Each player followed a young servant carrying messages between distant markets.
每位玩家都跟随一个年轻仆人，在相隔遥远的市场之间传递消息。
We wrote a long tale for every stop on the journey.
我们为旅程中的每一站都写了一个长故事。
The finished board looked splendid, but the rules were too tough for young children.
完成的棋盘看起来很漂亮，但规则对小孩子来说太难了。
Nobody wanted to buy it at our school sale.
学校义卖上，没有人想买它。
One teammate called herself a pioneer of simpler games and removed half the cards.
一位队友自称简单游戏的开拓者，拿掉了一半卡片。
Soon children were laughing as they raced to deliver their messages.
很快，孩子们一边争着送达消息，一边笑了起来。
We learned that a good idea must work for the people who use it.
我们明白了，好点子必须适合实际使用它的人。

stories.title: A Door That Opened Slowly
stories.picture: 动物救助站里，女孩静静坐在笼边，一只小狗从打开的门里探出头来。
paragraphs: Lately, I had been helping at an animal shelter after school.
最近，我放学后一直在一家动物救助站帮忙。
One small dog would not dare come near anyone.
有一只小狗不敢靠近任何人。
It paced back and forth at the far end of its pen.
它在围栏另一端来回踱步。
The keeper gave me one clear instruction: let the animal choose the distance.
饲养员给了我一条明确的指示：让动物自己决定保持多远的距离。
Whenever I sat nearby, I put down a little food and looked away.
每当我坐到附近，我都会放下一点食物，再把目光移开。
It did not matter if nothing happened that day.
即使那天毫无进展，也没有关系。
Eventually, I felt a wet nose touch the back of my hand.
终于，我感到一个湿湿的鼻子碰了碰我的手背。
I stayed still, knowing that trust grows better when nobody forces it.
我一动不动，因为我知道，没有强迫，信任才更容易生长。
